question: The 5th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games 2023 was hosted in January-February, 2023 by _______
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 5th Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) 2023 were hosted by Madhya Pradesh, from 30 January to 11 February 2023, mainly in Bhopal, with events also held in Gwalior, Indore, Ujjain and Jabalpur. (खेलो इंडिया यूथ गेम्स — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• This was the first time Madhya Pradesh hosted the Khelo India Youth Games; Maharashtra topped the medal tally at this edition.

 

• The official mascot of KIYG 2023 was 'Agni', inspired by the Barasingha (swamp deer), the state animal of Madhya Pradesh.

 

• Khelo India Youth Games is an annual national-level multi-disciplinary grassroots sporting event launched in 2018 to build a sports culture and unearth young talent across India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 4th Khelo India Youth Games (2022) were hosted by Haryana (Panchkula).

 

• The 6th Khelo India Youth Games (2025) were hosted by Bihar, with Patna as the main venue.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Did not host the 2023 edition of KIYG.

 

• Delhi (Option 2): Did not host the 2023 edition of KIYG.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): Did not host the 2023 edition of KIYG.

question: In a spread sheet, page orientation is changed through ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is page setup dialog box.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In spreadsheet software such as MS Excel, page orientation (Portrait or Landscape) is changed through the Page Setup dialog box, accessed via the Page Layout tab. (पृष्ठ अभिविन्यास — पेज सेटअप डायलॉग बॉक्स)

 

• The Page Setup dialog box also lets a user control margins, paper size, scaling and print area, in addition to orientation.

 

• It can be opened from the Page Layout ribbon by clicking the small arrow in the Page Setup group, or from the Print preview screen.

 

• Orientation settings affect only how the worksheet is laid out and printed; they do not alter the underlying data.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Page Setup dialog box in Excel has four tabs: Page, Margins, Header/Footer, and Sheet.

 

• 'Fit to' scaling, also found under Page Setup, is used to shrink or expand a worksheet to fit a specific number of pages when printing.

 

NOTE

 

• Format dialogue box (Option 2): Used mainly to format cell contents — number, font, alignment, border and fill — not page orientation.

 

• Print dialog box (Option 3): Used to select the printer, number of copies and print range; it does not control orientation directly.

 

• Paper dialog box (Option 4): Not a standard Excel dialog box; paper size is set within Page Setup, not a separate 'paper dialog box'.

question: Which of the following is a part of apical meristem found in roots.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Protoderm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The root apical meristem (RAM) gives rise to three primary meristems: protoderm, ground meristem, and procambium. (एपिकल विभज्योतक — प्रोटोडर्म)

 

• Protoderm is the outermost primary meristem; it later differentiates into the epidermis, the protective outer layer of the root.

 

• The ground meristem develops into the cortex and pith, while the procambium gives rise to the primary vascular tissues (xylem and phloem).

 

• Root apical meristem is protected by the root cap, unlike the shoot apical meristem, which has no such covering.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The shoot apical meristem (SAM), by contrast, gives rise to structures like leaf primordia and axillary buds, which are not features of root growth.

 

• Apical meristems are responsible for primary growth (increase in length) of both roots and shoots.

 

NOTE

 

• Leaf primordium (Option 2): A structure produced by the shoot apical meristem, which later develops into a leaf; it has no role in root growth.

 

• Differentiating vascular tissue (Option 3): This refers to tissue derived from the procambium as it matures, not a component of the apical meristem itself.

 

• Axillary bud (Option 4): Arises from the shoot apical meristem at the axil of a leaf; it is not associated with roots.

question: The institute established by Kaka Hathrasi in 1932 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangeet Karyalaya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kaka Hathrasi (Prabhu Lal Garg), the celebrated Hindi humour-satire (hasya-vyangya) poet, founded 'Sangeet Karyalaya' at Hathras, Uttar Pradesh, in 1932. (काका हाथरसी — संगीत कार्यालय)

 

• Sangeet Karyalaya is a well-known publishing house that has published works on Indian classical and folk music, as well as literary and satirical writing.

 

• Kaka Hathrasi is regarded as one of the pioneers of Hasya Kavi Sammelans (comic poetry gatherings) in Hindi literature and was honoured with the Padma Shri in 1983.

 

• He also founded the humour magazine 'Vinod' to promote satire and comic verse in Hindi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kaka Hathrasi's real name was Prabhu Lal Garg; 'Kaka Hathrasi' was his pen name, derived from his hometown Hathras.

 

• He is remembered for popularising the tradition of humorous poetry recitation (hasya kavita) at public gatherings across North India.

 

NOTE

 

• Music Art Centre (Option 1): Not the institute associated with Kaka Hathrasi; this is a distractor name.

 

• Swar Sangam Kendra (Option 2): Not the institute founded by Kaka Hathrasi; a similar-sounding distractor.

 

• Music Art Kendra (Option 4): Not the correct name of the institute; another similar-sounding distractor.

question: In an electrical circuit, the ammeter reading decreases to ________________ when the length of the wire is doubled.
solution_text:
The correct answer is one-half.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The resistance of a conductor is given by R = ρL/A, where ρ is resistivity, L is length and A is cross-sectional area. (प्रतिरोध सूत्र — R = ρL/A)

 

• Since R is directly proportional to L, doubling the length doubles the resistance of the wire, assuming the material and cross-sectional area stay unchanged.

 

• By Ohm's Law, I = V/R; with the supply voltage V held constant, doubling R halves the current I.

 

• Since an ammeter reads the current flowing through the circuit, its reading falls to one-half of its original value.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• If instead the cross-sectional area (thickness) of the wire were doubled while length stayed the same, resistance would halve, and current would double.

 

• An ammeter is always connected in series in a circuit and ideally has very low (near-zero) resistance so it does not itself alter the current being measured.

 

NOTE

 

• One-sixth (Option 1): Does not follow from R ∝ L; this would require a much larger, unjustified change in resistance.

 

• One-fourth (Option 3): This would be the result only if the length were increased four times, not doubled.

 

• One-third (Option 4): Does not correspond to a simple doubling of length under R ∝ L; incorrect proportional relationship.

question: Which of the following steps is used to format a cell in an MS Excel Spreadsheet?
option_2: Select cell → Right click → Format cell
solution_text:
The correct answer is Select cell → Right click → Format cell.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS Excel, a cell is formatted by first selecting it, then right-clicking to open the context menu, and choosing 'Format Cells...'. (सेल फॉर्मेट करना — Format Cells)

 

• The Format Cells dialog box opens with tabs for Number, Alignment, Font, Border, Fill, and Protection, allowing complete control over how the cell's content is displayed.

 

• The same dialog box can also be opened using the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + 1 after selecting a cell, or via the Home tab's Font/Alignment/Number launcher icons.

 

• 'Format Cells' is distinct from Excel's general 'Format' menu options used for rows, columns, or sheet-level settings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Excel also offers Conditional Formatting, which automatically formats cells based on their values using rules set by the user.

 

• The Format Painter tool can be used to quickly copy formatting from one cell to another without reopening the Format Cells dialog box.

 

NOTE

 

• Menu → Select cell → Format (Option 1): Reverses the correct order; a cell must first be selected before any formatting option can be applied to it.

 

• Select cell → View → Format cell (Option 3): The 'View' tab in Excel controls window/display settings (gridlines, zoom, freeze panes), not cell formatting.

 

• View → Select cell → Format (Option 4): Incorrect sequence and incorrect menu; formatting a cell does not begin from the View tab.

question:
Match the following ports with their related states correctly.

Ports: 1. Mormugao port  2. Paradip Port  3. Haldia Port  4. Tuticorin port

States: a. West Bengal  b. Odisha  c. Tamil Nadu  d. Goa
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-d, 2-b, 3-a, 4-c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mormugao Port is located in Goa (1-d), on the estuary of the Zuari river, and is a major port for iron ore exports. (मोरमुगाओ पोर्ट — गोवा)

 

• Paradip Port is located in Odisha (2-b), on the Bay of Bengal at the mouth of the Mahanadi river, and is one of India's major iron-ore and coal handling ports.

 

• Haldia Port is located in West Bengal (3-a), on the Hooghly river, and functions as a satellite port of Kolkata Port.

 

• Tuticorin (V.O. Chidambaranar) Port is located in Tamil Nadu (4-c), on the Gulf of Mannar, and is a major container and cargo hub in South India.

 

• Together this gives the correct matching 1-d, 2-b, 3-a, 4-c.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has 12 major ports, including Mumbai, JNPT (Nhava Sheva), Kandla (Deendayal), Kolkata, Chennai, Cochin, Vishakhapatnam, New Mangalore, Ennore (Kamarajar) and the four named above.

 

• Major ports are administered by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways under the Major Port Authorities Act, 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (1-b, 2-d, 3-c, 4-a): Incorrectly swaps Mormugao and Paradip's states with Haldia and Tuticorin's, mismatching every pairing.

 

• Option 2 (1-a, 2-b, 3-d, 4-c): Correctly pairs Paradip-Odisha and Tuticorin-Tamil Nadu but wrongly swaps Mormugao (Goa) and Haldia (West Bengal).

 

• Option 4 (1-b, 2-d, 3-a, 4-c): Correctly pairs Haldia-West Bengal and Tuticorin-Tamil Nadu but wrongly swaps Mormugao (Goa) and Paradip (Odisha).

question: Which is the first state to receive rain from the Monsoon in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Southwest Monsoon first strikes the Indian mainland at the coast of Kerala, typically around 1 June each year. (मानसून की पहली दस्तक — केरल)

 

• The monsoon arrives in two branches — the Arabian Sea branch (which hits Kerala first) and the Bay of Bengal branch (which strikes the northeastern states, first reaching areas near Assam/Meghalaya).

 

• From Kerala, the Arabian Sea branch advances further, reaching Karnataka, Goa, and Maharashtra in the following days.

 

• The India Meteorological Department (IMD) formally declares the 'onset of monsoon' when it hits Kerala, marking the start of India's rainy season.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mawsynram and Cherrapunji in Meghalaya are among the wettest places on Earth, receiving extremely heavy rainfall from the Bay of Bengal branch of the monsoon.

 

• The Southwest Monsoon typically withdraws from India starting in September, retreating first from northwest India and last from the southern peninsula.

 

NOTE

 

• Goa (Option 2): Receives monsoon rains after Kerala and Karnataka, as the Arabian Sea branch moves northward along the west coast.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): Receives monsoon rainfall later than Kerala, as the monsoon progresses along the coast and inland.

 

• Karnataka (Option 4): Receives monsoon rain shortly after Kerala, but Kerala is struck first.

question: In which of the following cities was the Asian Wrestling Championship 2023 held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Astana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2023 Asian Wrestling Championships were held in Astana, Kazakhstan, in April 2023. (एशियाई कुश्ती चैंपियनशिप 2023 — अस्ताना, कजाकिस्तान)

 

• The event was originally scheduled to be hosted by New Delhi, India, but the venue was shifted to Astana after Pakistani wrestlers could not be guaranteed visas in time.

 

• Indian wrestlers won several medals at the 2023 edition, including gold medals in freestyle and Greco-Roman categories.

 

• The championship is organised by the United World Wrestling (UWW) Asian body and features freestyle, Greco-Roman and women's wrestling categories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2024 Asian Wrestling Championships were held in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan.

 

• India has a strong wrestling tradition, with wrestlers like Vinesh Phogat, Bajrang Punia and Sakshi Malik representing the country at major international events during this period.

 

NOTE

 

• Mumbai (Option 1): Did not host the 2023 Asian Wrestling Championships; the originally planned Indian host city was New Delhi, not Mumbai, and even that venue was changed.

 

• Tokyo (Option 3): Did not host the 2023 Asian Wrestling Championships.

 

• Karachi (Option 4): Did not host the 2023 Asian Wrestling Championships.

question: Federalism in the Indian constitutional context means:
option_1: the existence only one level of government in the country
option_2: the existence of one nation one government in the country
option_3: the existence of states in the country
option_4: the existence of more than one level of government in the country
solution_text:
The correct answer is the existence of more than one level of government in the country.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Federalism refers to a system of government in which power is constitutionally divided between a central (Union) authority and constituent units (states), i.e., more than one level of government operating simultaneously. (संघवाद — एक से अधिक सरकार स्तर)

 

• India's Constitution establishes a quasi-federal / 'federal with a strong unitary bias' structure, with a clear division of powers through the Union List, State List and Concurrent List (Seventh Schedule).

 

• India, in fact, has three levels of government: the Union (Central) Government, State Governments, and Local Self-Government (Panchayats and Municipalities, added via the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, 1992).

 

• Federalism ensures shared sovereignty, with both levels of government deriving authority directly from the Constitution rather than from each other.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India is often described as having a 'federal structure with unitary features', since in emergencies (Articles 352, 356, 360) the Centre can override state autonomy.

 

• The term 'Union of States' is used in Article 1 of the Indian Constitution rather than 'Federation', reflecting that the states cannot secede from the Union.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Describes a unitary, not federal, system, where only a single level of government exists.

 

• Option 2: 'One nation, one government' also describes a unitary system, the opposite of federalism.

 

• Option 3: Merely stating that states exist does not capture federalism; federalism is specifically about the division of governmental power between levels, not just the existence of states.

question: Which of the following schemes is related to minimising the use of chemical fertilisers, given in the Union Budget 2023-24?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PM Pranam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• PM-PRANAM (Prime Minister Programme for Restoration, Awareness, Nourishment and Amelioration of Mother Earth) was announced in the Union Budget 2023-24 to promote balanced and reduced use of chemical fertilisers and encourage alternative fertilisers. (पीएम-प्रणाम — रासायनिक उर्वरकों में कमी)

 

• The scheme incentivises state governments by sharing the fertiliser subsidy savings with them when they cut down on chemical fertiliser consumption.

 

• It supports the promotion of organic and natural farming practices, aligned with India's broader sustainable agriculture goals.

 

• PM-PRANAM does not have a separate budget of its own; it is funded through savings from the existing fertiliser subsidy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Budget 2023-24 initiatives for agriculture included the Atmanirbhar Clean Plant Programme and the Agriculture Accelerator Fund for agri-startups.

 

• Excessive chemical fertiliser use is linked to soil degradation, groundwater contamination and greenhouse gas emissions, which schemes like PM-PRANAM aim to mitigate.

 

NOTE

 

• PM DevINE (Option 2): 'Prime Minister's Development Initiative for North East Region', announced in Budget 2022-23 to fund infrastructure and social development projects in the Northeast; unrelated to fertilisers.

 

• SEED Scheme (Option 3): 'Skill India, Employment and Entrepreneurship Development' related initiatives focus on skilling and livelihoods, not fertiliser use.

 

• PM Shri (Option 4): 'PM Schools for Rising India' is a scheme to upgrade schools as model institutions; unrelated to agriculture or fertilisers.

question: Jagoi and Cholom are two divisions in the Indian classical dance form of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Manipuri dance, one of the eight Indian classical dance forms, is broadly divided into two categories: Jagoi (graceful, lyrical, devotional dance) and Cholom (vigorous, martial/drum dance performed mainly by men). (मणिपुरी नृत्य — जागोई और चोलोम)

 

• Manipuri dance originates from Manipur and is deeply intertwined with Vaishnavite themes, especially the Ras Lila depicting the life of Radha and Krishna.

 

• Jagoi includes sub-forms like Ras Leela and is characterised by gentle, flowing movements, subtle facial expressions and minimal footwork noise.

 

• Cholom, on the other hand, includes forms like Pung Cholom (drum dance) and Dhol Cholom, marked by energetic movements and acrobatics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The eight recognised Indian classical dance forms are Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

• Manipuri dance emphasises soft, rounded body movements without sharp jerks or stamping, distinguishing it from more percussive forms like Kathak.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathak (Option 1): A North Indian classical dance form characterised by rhythmic footwork (tatkar) and spins (chakkars); Jagoi and Cholom are not its divisions.

 

• Kathakali (Option 3): A classical dance-drama from Kerala known for elaborate makeup and costumes; unrelated to Jagoi and Cholom.

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 4): A classical dance form from Tamil Nadu, structured around the margam sequence; Jagoi and Cholom are not part of its tradition.

question: Which of the following is NOT any position in the Basketball sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is All rounder.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Standard basketball playing positions are: Point Guard, Shooting Guard, Small Forward, Power Forward, and Centre — five positions in total. (बास्केटबॉल पोजीशन — ऑल राउंडर नहीं)

 

• 'All-rounder' is a term used in cricket to describe a player skilled in both batting and bowling; it is not a recognised basketball position.

 

• The Point Guard is typically the primary ball-handler and playmaker, responsible for setting up plays.

 

• The Shooting Guard focuses on perimeter scoring, while the Small Forward is a versatile player contributing to both scoring and defence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The two remaining basketball positions not listed among the options are the Power Forward (plays near the basket, rebounding and inside scoring) and the Centre (the tallest player, dominant near the basket).

 

• A basketball team has 5 players on court at a time, one for each of these five positions.

 

NOTE

 

• Point guard (Option 1): A genuine, recognised basketball position; hence not the answer.

 

• Shooting guard (Option 2): A genuine, recognised basketball position; hence not the answer.

 

• Small forward (Option 3): A genuine, recognised basketball position; hence not the answer.

question: As of August, 2023, which of the following states has India's first fully functionally literate district?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mandla district, in Madhya Pradesh, became India's first fully 'functionally literate' district, an achievement announced around August 2023. (मंडला जिला — मध्य प्रदेश, प्रथम पूर्ण रूप से क्रियात्मक साक्षर जिला)

 

• 'Functional literacy' goes beyond basic literacy — it means a person can read, write and perform basic arithmetic well enough to use these skills in daily life and livelihood activities.

 

• This achievement was made under the Union Ministry of Education's 'Ullas – Nav Bharat Saksharta Karyakram' (New India Literacy Programme), aimed at achieving universal functional literacy.

 

• Mandla, a tribal-dominated district, was recognised for successfully covering its non-literate adult population through targeted literacy drives.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The New India Literacy Programme (ULLAS) was launched for the period 2022-2027, targeting non-literate persons aged 15 years and above.

 

• Mizoram was later declared India's first fully literate state in 2025 under related literacy initiatives.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Not the state where India's first fully functionally literate district (Mandla) is located.

 

• Kerala (Option 3): Known for very high general literacy rates historically, but the specific 'first fully functionally literate district' distinction (Mandla) belongs to Madhya Pradesh, not Kerala.

 

• Goa (Option 4): Not the state associated with this particular distinction.

question: The President of India appointed __________ as the Governor of Karnataka in July 2021.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thaawar Chand Gehlot.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thaawar Chand Gehlot was appointed Governor of Karnataka by the President of India in July 2021. (थावरचंद गहलोत — कर्नाटक के राज्यपाल)

 

• He previously served as the Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment in the Government of India before his gubernatorial appointment.

 

• Prior to Karnataka, he had also briefly served as Governor of Madhya Pradesh in 2021.

 

• Karnataka's Raj Bhavan is located in Bengaluru, the state capital.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar later served as Governor of Bihar and subsequently of Himachal Pradesh and Kerala.

 

• Hari Babu Kambhampati has served as Governor of Mizoram, while Mangubhai Chhaganbhai Patel has served as Governor of Madhya Pradesh and Odisha.

 

NOTE

 

• Hari Babu Kambhampati (Option 1): Served as Governor of Mizoram, not Karnataka, in this period.

 

• Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar (Option 3): Was Governor of Bihar around this time, not Karnataka.

 

• Mangubhai Chhaganbhai Patel (Option 4): Served as Governor of Madhya Pradesh and later Odisha, not Karnataka.

question: In Hindustani classical music, according to Vishnu Narayana Bhatkhande, how many thaats are the origins of ragas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande, a pioneering musicologist, classified all Hindustani classical ragas as originating from 10 parent scales called 'thaats'. (विष्णु नारायण भातखंडे — 10 थाट)

 

• The 10 thaats are: Bilawal, Kalyan, Khamaj, Bhairav, Poorvi, Marwa, Kafi, Asavari, Bhairavi, and Todi.

 

• A thaat is essentially a parent scale (a specific arrangement of seven notes) from which multiple ragas sharing the same notes are derived.

 

• Bhatkhande's thaat system is the most widely accepted classification framework used in Hindustani (North Indian) classical music theory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In Carnatic (South Indian) classical music, the analogous concept is the Melakarta system, which recognises 72 parent scales (Melakarta ragas) — this is the source of the '72' figure in Option 2, but that applies to Carnatic, not Hindustani, music.

 

• Bhatkhande also authored the multi-volume 'Kramik Pustak Malika', a foundational text systematising Hindustani classical music.

 

NOTE

 

• 52 (Option 1): Not a recognised number of thaats or ragas in any standard classification system.

 

• 72 (Option 2): This is the number of Melakarta ragas in Carnatic music, not the number of Bhatkhande's Hindustani thaats.

 

• 20 (Option 4): Not the correct number of thaats identified by Bhatkhande.

question: The Prarthana Samaj was established in ________ by Dr. Atma Ram Pandurang.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay (now Mumbai) in 1867 by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang, with support from social reformers like M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar. (प्रार्थना समाज — बंबई)

 

• It was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj and aimed to promote monotheism, social reform, and the eradication of practices like caste discrimination and child marriage.

 

• The Samaj worked towards causes such as widow remarriage, women's education, and inter-caste dining, while retaining certain Hindu religious practices unlike the more radical Brahmo Samaj.

 

• Mahadev Govind Ranade became one of its most influential leaders, significantly expanding its social reform agenda in Maharashtra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brahmo Samaj, which inspired the Prarthana Samaj, was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Calcutta in 1828.

 

• The Theosophical Society later moved its international headquarters to Adyar, Madras (Chennai) in 1882, under Annie Besant's leadership.

 

NOTE

 

• Calcutta (Option 2): This is where the Brahmo Samaj was founded, not the Prarthana Samaj.

 

• Adyar (Option 3): This is associated with the headquarters of the Theosophical Society, not the Prarthana Samaj.

 

• Delhi (Option 4): Not the founding location of the Prarthana Samaj.

question: Where is the oldest centre of lace work located in Gujarat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jamnagar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jamnagar, in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, is recognised as the oldest centre of lace-making in the state. (फीता कला — जामनगर)

 

• Lace work here traditionally involves crocheting delicate cotton or silk threads into decorative borders and trims, used on garments and household linen.

 

• Jamnagar is also well known for other crafts such as Bandhani (tie-dye) textiles and traditional brasswork.

 

• The lace craft of Jamnagar reflects a long-standing local artisan tradition passed down through generations of craftswomen.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gujarat is home to a wide range of textile crafts, including Patola weaving (Patan), Bandhani (Jamnagar/Bhuj), and mirror-work embroidery (Kutch).

 

• Kutch is more prominently known for its intricate embroidery and mirror work (Abhla Bharat) rather than lace-making specifically.

 

NOTE

 

• Ahmedabad (Option 1): Known for crafts such as block printing and textiles generally, but not identified as the oldest lace-work centre.

 

• Rajkot (Option 2): Not recognised as the oldest lace-work centre in Gujarat.

 

• Kutch (Option 4): Famous for embroidery and mirror work, but the oldest lace-work centre is specifically Jamnagar.

question: The Chau dancers of ___________ organise a festival named Chau-Jhumur Utsav, where an open stage is designed for the performance by Chau groups.
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chau-Jhumur Utsav is organised by Chau dancers of West Bengal, particularly in the Purulia district, where the Purulia Chhau dance tradition is prominent. (छऊ-झुमुर उत्सव — पश्चिम बंगाल)

 

• The festival features an open-air stage (chandimandap-style ground), allowing large audiences to watch the vigorous, masked Chhau dance performances along with Jhumur folk songs.

 

• Purulia Chhau is a masked martial dance form depicting stories from epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata, accompanied by traditional drums like the dhol and dhamsa.

 

• Chhau dance has been inscribed by UNESCO on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity (2010).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• There are three regional styles of Chhau: Purulia Chhau (West Bengal), Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).

 

• Mayurbhanj Chhau is unique in being performed without masks, unlike the Purulia and Seraikella styles.

 

NOTE

 

• Chhattisgarh (Option 2): Not associated with the Chau-Jhumur Utsav or a recognised Chhau tradition.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 3): Home to the Seraikella Chhau style, but the Chau-Jhumur Utsav specifically is organised in West Bengal.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): Not associated with Chhau dance traditions or this festival.

question: In which year was the 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana' launched by the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2020.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana (ABRY) was launched by the Government of India on 1 October 2020 to boost employment generation during the post-COVID-19 economic recovery. (आत्मनिर्भर भारत रोजगार योजना — 2020)

 

• Under the scheme, the Government contributes both the employer's and employee's EPF contributions (or just the employee's share, depending on establishment size) for two years, for new employees earning less than ₹15,000 per month.

 

• It is implemented by the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) and aims to incentivise employers to hire more workers and formalise employment.

 

• The scheme was part of the broader Aatmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India) package of economic stimulus measures announced in 2020.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• ABRY was originally intended to run until 30 June 2021, but its registration deadline was extended multiple times, eventually up to 31 March 2022.

 

• Other components of the Aatmanirbhar Bharat package included the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) for MSMEs.

 

NOTE

 

• 2022 (Option 2): Not the launch year; 2022 falls within the scheme's later extension period, not its launch.

 

• 2015 (Option 3): Too early; the scheme is a COVID-19-era measure and did not exist in 2015.

 

• 2010 (Option 4): Not the launch year; the scheme did not exist at that time.

question: Which of the following years were considered plan holidays in Independent India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1966-1969.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The period 1966-1969 is known as the 'Plan Holiday' in India's Five-Year Plan history, when three Annual Plans were implemented instead of a Five-Year Plan. (योजना अवकाश — 1966-1969)

 

• This break followed the failure of the Third Five-Year Plan (1961-66), caused by the Indo-Pak War of 1965, severe drought/famine, and devaluation of the rupee.

 

• During the Plan Holiday, India shifted focus to annual planning, allowing flexibility in resource allocation each year amid the economic crisis.

 

• The Fourth Five-Year Plan eventually began in 1969, after the Plan Holiday ended.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74) focused on the objectives of 'growth with stability' and progress towards self-reliance, and included the nationalisation of 14 major banks in 1969.

 

• India has had multiple gaps/annual-plan periods in its planning history; the 1966-69 Plan Holiday is the most well-known and frequently tested.

 

NOTE

 

• 1964-1967 (Option 1): Not the correct period; it overlaps with but does not match the actual Plan Holiday years.

 

• 1990-1992 (Option 2): This period saw the transition following the Eighth Plan's delay (due to political instability and the 1991 economic crisis), not the original 'Plan Holiday'.

 

• 1969-1972 (Option 3): Incorrect; the Fourth Five-Year Plan had already begun in 1969, ending the Plan Holiday period, not starting it.

question: _____ is defined as excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings during a fiscal year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fiscal deficit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fiscal deficit is defined as the excess of the government's total expenditure over its total receipts (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts), excluding borrowings, during a fiscal year. (राजकोषीय घाटा — व्यय, प्राप्तियों से अधिक)

 

• It represents the total amount the government needs to borrow during the year to meet its expenditure, and is a key indicator of the government's overall financial health.

 

• Fiscal deficit is usually expressed as a percentage of GDP; India's fiscal deficit targets are set out under the FRBM Act (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003).

 

• Formula: Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt Capital Receipts).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts, and reflects the shortfall in the government's current (day-to-day) account.

 

• Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit − Interest payments; it shows the deficit excluding the burden of past borrowings.

 

NOTE

 

• Income deficit (Option 2): Not a standard term used in Indian public-finance/budgetary terminology for this concept.

 

• Structural deficit (Option 3): Refers to a deficit that persists even when the economy is at full employment/potential output; it is a different macroeconomic concept, not this standard budget definition.

 

• Gross Primary deficit (Option 4): Refers to the fiscal deficit minus interest payments, a related but distinct concept from the definition given in the question.

question: Part IV A of the Indian Constitution is related to _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fundamental Duties.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution deals with Fundamental Duties, laid out in a single article, Article 51-A. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — भाग IV-A, अनुच्छेद 51-A)

 

• Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

• Originally there were 10 Fundamental Duties; an 11th duty (regarding the duty of parents/guardians to provide education to children aged 6-14) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

• Fundamental Duties are not legally enforceable in a court of law, unlike Fundamental Rights, but serve as a constant reminder of citizens' moral obligations to the nation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Directive Principles of State Policy are covered in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Constitution.

 

• Fundamental Rights are covered in Part III (Articles 12-35), while matters of Citizenship are dealt with in Part II (Articles 5-11).

 

NOTE

 

• Directive Principles of State Policy (Option 1): These are covered under Part IV, not Part IV-A, of the Constitution.

 

• Fundamental Rights (Option 3): These are covered under Part III of the Constitution, not Part IV-A.

 

• Citizenship (Option 4): This subject is dealt with in Part II of the Constitution, not Part IV-A.

question: Which of the following statements most accurately describes the planet Saturn?
option_1: Its surface is reddish in colour.
option_2: It is a gas giant made up mostly of hydrogen and helium and the density is less than that of water.
option_3: It was the seventh planet discovered in the Solar System.
option_4: Its cloud-like outer regions consist of methane in the gaseous form and ammonia in crystalline form.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is a gas giant made up mostly of hydrogen and helium and the density is less than that of water.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saturn is the second-largest planet in the Solar System and a gas giant, composed predominantly of hydrogen and helium, similar in composition to Jupiter. (शनि ग्रह — गैस दानव, जल से कम घनत्व)

 

• Saturn's average density is about 0.687 g/cm³, which is less than the density of water (1 g/cm³) — meaning Saturn would theoretically float if placed in a large enough body of water.

 

• Saturn is famous for its extensive and prominent ring system, made mostly of ice particles with some rocky debris and dust.

 

• It is the sixth planet from the Sun and has been known since ancient times, being visible to the naked eye.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Saturn has the second-most moons of any planet in the Solar System, with Titan being its largest moon, notable for its thick atmosphere.

 

• Saturn's rotation is very fast (about 10.7 hours per day), causing it to be visibly oblate (flattened at the poles).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Saturn's cloud tops appear pale yellow/golden, not reddish; a reddish surface is more characteristic of Mars.

 

• Option 3: Saturn has been known since antiquity and was not 'discovered' in a chronological sequence of planet discoveries the way Uranus or Neptune were.

 

• Option 4: The description of cloud-like outer regions with gaseous methane and crystalline ammonia in specific layered form matches the atmosphere of Uranus/Jupiter-type descriptions more precisely than the standard description of Saturn used in the correct option.

question: Who defeated Mohammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain fought in the year 1191?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prithviraj Chauhan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The First Battle of Tarain, fought in 1191 CE, was won by Prithviraj Chauhan (Prithviraj III), the Chahamana (Chauhan) ruler of Ajmer and Delhi, who defeated Muhammad Ghori. (तराइन का प्रथम युद्ध, 1191 — पृथ्वीराज चौहान)

 

• Ghori was severely wounded in this battle and forced to retreat, but Prithviraj chose not to press his advantage further at the time.

 

• Just a year later, in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), Muhammad Ghori returned with a larger force and defeated Prithviraj Chauhan, marking a turning point that paved the way for Turkic rule in North India.

 

• Prithviraj Chauhan is remembered in Indian history and folklore (including the epic poem 'Prithviraj Raso' by Chand Bardai) as a valiant Rajput king.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Following his victory in 1192, Muhammad Ghori's general Qutb-ud-din Aibak went on to lay the foundations of the Delhi Sultanate, later establishing the Mamluk (Slave) Dynasty in 1206.

 

• The Tarain (Taraori) battlefield is located near present-day Karnal, Haryana.

 

NOTE

 

• Vasudev (Option 2): Not associated with the Battles of Tarain; a distractor name.

 

• Yashovarman (Option 3): A historical ruler from an earlier era (Kannauj), unrelated to the 1191 Battle of Tarain.

 

• Vidyadhar (Option 4): A ruler of the Chandela dynasty from an earlier period, unrelated to the 1191 Battle of Tarain.
